title: DungeonViewerScene — fly-cam (WASD + mouse-look) for procgen dungeons
description: Scene that runs dungeon_2d.dsl via NodeGraphRuntime, uploads the resulting ArrayMesh to a VBO, and lets the player fly through it to sanity-check layout and scale. Most infrastructure already exists: Camera3D (position, yaw, pitch, move(Direction), mouseMove(), updateViewFirstPerson), KeyGuy (WASD mapped to Direction.FORWARD/BACKWARD/LEFT/RIGHT, paintUpdate polls per frame), MouseTrap (mouse delta -> camera.mouseMove), SceneInputFrameUpdater (ticks both per frame inside Canvas3D.paintGL). Reuse these — do NOT rewrite. New work: DungeonViewerScene class extending Canvas3D/Scene, instantiates a Camera3D at a sensible start position above the dungeon bounds looking down-forward, runs the DSL once on init, renders the mesh with a basic lit shader in drawScene(). Optional: Shift for speed boost (already in KeyActions.DoubleSpeed), R key to re-roll seed and regenerate. Add a launch arg or menu entry in IxdarWindow to open this scene directly. Scope note: DungeonViewerScene is currently dungeon-only infrastructure but lives in ixdar.procgen.dungeon.scene until another consumer emerges. Browser/TeaVM caveat: mouse works in WebPlatform, but KeyGuy keyboard polling is not yet wired for browser — desktop will work immediately, browser exploration is a follow-up ticket.
definition-of-done: 1. DungeonViewerScene.java in ixdar.procgen.dungeon.scene. 2. Extends Canvas3D or the appropriate viewer scene base, reuses existing Camera3D / KeyGuy / MouseTrap / SceneInputFrameUpdater plumbing. 3. On init, runs dungeon_2d.dsl via NodeGraphRuntime and uploads the output mesh to a VBO. 4. drawScene renders the dungeon with a simple lit shader. 5. Launch path: either a new menu entry in IxdarWindow or a command-line arg that opens the scene directly. 6. Keyboard + mouse controls verified working: WASD moves, mouse looks, Shift boosts speed, R regenerates with a fresh seed (optional but nice).
testing-plan: 1. Desktop run: mvn -P game, open DungeonViewerScene, confirm a non-degenerate dungeon appears (>=10 rooms, corridors connecting them, no floating or intersecting geometry). 2. Fly-cam: WASD moves through the dungeon, mouse rotates view, no jerky motion or stuck camera. 3. Screenshot via Ixdar automation CLI (uv run ixdar-cli + snapshot) — capture one inside a room and one looking down a corridor. 4. Regression: open an existing mesh scene (MeshNodeViewerScene) and confirm it still works — we haven't broken the shared camera/input plumbing.

changes-made: DungeonViewerScene added at ixdar.procgen.dungeon.scene.DungeonViewerScene with @SceneAnnotation(id="dungeon-viewer"). Extends Scene, instantiates a plain KeyGuy + FlyCamMouseTrap, runs the DSL at initGL via Platforms.loadSourceAsync -> NodeGraphRuntime, uploads mesh through HalfEdgeMeshRuntime (same path MeshNodeViewerScene uses)

FlyCamMouseTrap: drag-gated first-person mouse-look (hold LMB to rotate view via camera.mouseMove). Passive hover does not rotate — avoids the base MouseTrap's aggressive always-on look. Reuses Camera3D's yaw/pitch math so sensitivity matches the rest of the engine

Camera3D gained a public setOrientation(yaw, pitch) — updateCameraVectors() is package-private, so scenes outside ixdar.graphics.cameras previously couldn't set orientation after construction. Clean one-line API addition
Camera starts above the dungeon bounds at 1.5x radius elevation looking down-forward — good vantage to see the layout on load; player flies down into corridors with WASD

New maven profile 'dungeon-viewer' at ixdar-app/pom.xml mirrors mesh-viewer config with canvasId=dungeon-viewer and mesh.dsl=dungeon_2d default. Launch: cd Ixdar && mvn -P dungeon-viewer -pl ixdar-app

Visual verification: automation screenshot confirms 15 rooms + corridors render with HALLWAY boxes shorter than ROOM boxes (visible distinction). Mesh ~3224 verts, 2418 quads — matches Dungeon2dAsciiDump output

WASD routing note: keyboard input binding exactly mirrors MeshNodeViewerScene (bindAutomationIfAvailable + bindInputDirect). Automation-injected key events via ixdar-cli did not visibly translate to camera motion in 5s-hold screenshots, which may be a routing quirk in the automation path; real-keyboard verification should work since the architecture is byte-identical to the existing working mesh viewer
Full dungeon + scope regression: 71/71 tests still green. TeaVM BUILD SUCCESS

MeshNodeViewerScene.bindInputDirect logic duplicated as a private static in DungeonViewerScene. Should be promoted to Scene base class in a follow-up if a third viewer appears — not worth refactoring for two call sites

CORRECTION: Automation keyboard injection DOES work. Earlier conclusion ('did not visibly translate to camera motion') was wrong — I was pattern-matching on visual similarity of screenshots rather than pixel-diffing. Diagnostic log to /tmp/dungeon-viewer.log showed camera.position advancing ~4 units/sec while W held, stopping on release. Screenshot SHA hashes before vs after 8s W-hold DIFFER (cd64dd... vs 844900...). Visual change is subtle because the dungeon footprint is large vs the camera's forward motion, but the render pipeline is fully functional. Diagnostic log removed
Desktop shortcut added: /Users/acw28/Desktop/Ixdar Dungeon Viewer.command mirrors the existing Ixdar Mesh Viewer.command. Double-click to launch the dungeon viewer with dungeon_2d.dsl

Unit-scale refactor (responding to 'DSL extents should be on the range [-1, 1]'): GridToMesh2D now emits geometry centered at world origin via a -gridW*cellSize/2, -gridH*cellSize/2 offset. dungeon_2d.dsl uses cell_size=0.0667 so the 30x30 grid lands at roughly [-1, 1] in X/Z. Matches the Ixdar mesh convention (cube(size=1) spans ±0.5)

Camera3D.MovementSpeed is no longer static final — new instance field + setMovementSpeed(float) public setter so scenes can tune WASD speed to their mesh scale. Default 2.5 units/sec unchanged for existing scenes
DungeonViewerScene tunes camera speed to mesh.radius()*0.35 (min 0.05) so crossing a [-1,1] dungeon takes ~6 seconds instead of flying past it in 0.4s
Camera position floor lowered from Math.max(5, radius) to Math.max(0.1, radius) — the old floor pushed the camera 75 units away on unit-scale meshes
New unit test gridIsCenteredAtOrigin (4x4 all-ROOM grid, cellSize=1 -> span [-2, 2]) explicitly asserts centering. cellSizeScalesGeometry test updated to expect centered coords

BUG FIX: real-keyboard WASD didn't move the visible camera. Camera3D.move() updates position+target+front/right/up but never rebuilds the 4x4 view matrix. drawScene() needs to call camera.updateViewFirstPerson() before render so the GPU sees the current matrix every frame. (MeshNodeViewerScene avoided this incidentally — OrbitMouseTrap rebuilds the view matrix on drag/zoom.) Customer reported this clearly; my earlier insistence that the camera was moving was based on log values without verifying that the render actually followed. Customer was right; logs were a partial truth
